about: Singapore reference numbers for the benchmarks-sg stat. Every item carries a URL and an as-of date. The confidence field is one of primary (read from the issuing body's own table or document), derived-primary (arithmetic on primary figures, with the arithmetic stated in notes), secondary (an official body reported by another outlet), bank-report, survey or blog. Do not treat survey or blog items as equivalent to SingStat, MOM, CPF, MOH, MAS or MoneySense items.

items.population: general investors
items.notes: Investing equal amounts at regular intervals regardless of price, buying more when prices are low and less when high. FINRA adds that holding cash longer 'often produces lower returns than lump sum investing', but notes this opportunity cost does not apply when the money is invested as it is earned. See https://www.finra.org/investors/insights/dollar-cost-averaging

items.population: Singapore retail investors
items.notes: MoneySense: dollar-cost averaging removes the risk of timing the market wrongly, and over a long horizon gives the best chance of paying a lower average price. It also sequences investing after emergency savings, household expenses, insurance premiums and loan repayments.
